questions.text: A one-way solid concrete slab is simply supported over a clear span of 5 meters (Grade 40 steel). What is the minimum slab thickness required by NSCP to control deflection without explicit calculation?

rationale.a: 200 mm = L/25, which is not a standard NSCP ratio for slabs.
rationale.c: 300 mm = L/16.7, which is between slab and beam ratios.
rationale.d: 400 mm = L/12.5, which is thicker than required.
rationale.correct: For simply supported one-way solid slabs, NSCP 2015 Table 409-1 specifies minimum thickness = L/20. For 5 m span: 5000/20 = 250 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An interior span of a continuous one-way solid slab is 6 meters long. What is the minimum slab thickness per NSCP deflection control?

rationale.a: 250 mm = L/24, which is for one-end-continuous slabs.
rationale.b: 300 mm = L/20, which is for simply supported slabs.
rationale.d: 240 mm = L/25, which is not a standard NSCP ratio.
rationale.correct: For both-ends-continuous one-way solid slabs, NSCP Table 9.5.1 specifies minimum thickness = L/28. For 6 m span: 6000/28 ≈ 214 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Compare minimum thickness requirements for a simply supported element: one-way solid slab vs. ribbed beam, both with 6 m span and Grade 60 steel.

options.text: Slab L/20 = 300 mm; Beam L/16 = 375 mm (beam thicker)
Slab L/20 = 300 mm; Beam L/20 = 300 mm (same thickness)
Slab L/16 = 375 mm; Beam L/20 = 300 mm (slab thicker)
Slab L/28 = 214 mm; Beam L/8 = 750 mm (beam thicker)

rationale.b: Solid slab and ribbed beam do NOT use the same ratio.
rationale.c: Reverses the values; slab is L/20 (300 mm), not L/16.
rationale.d: Confuses cantilever ratios (L/10 for slab, L/8 for beam) with simply supported.
rationale.correct: Simply supported solid slab = L/20 (6000/20 = 300 mm). Simply supported ribbed beam = L/16 (6000/16 = 375 mm). Beams require more stiffness because they carry concentrated loads; slabs are more efficient for distributed loads (NSCP Table 9.5.1).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A one-way continuous ribbed (joist) slab is supported at both ends over a 7 m interior span. What is the minimum joist depth per NSCP?

rationale.a: 438 mm = L/16, which is for simply supported ribbed slabs.
rationale.b: 378 mm = L/18.5, which is for one-end-continuous ribbed slabs.
rationale.d: 875 mm = L/8, which is for cantilever ribbed slabs.
rationale.correct: For both-ends-continuous ribbed/joist slabs, NSCP Table 9.5.1 specifies minimum depth = L/21. For 7 m span: 7000/21 ≈ 333 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A one-way solid slab with a 4 m simply supported span is initially designed at thickness = 200 mm per L/20 ratio. A code reviewer notes this is below minimum. What is the correct minimum thickness?

options.text: 160 mm (thinner than specified, not meeting the minimum thickness required for structural integrity)
250 mm (per L/16, more conservative, ensuring compliance with additional safety margins)
The reviewer is wrong; 200 mm satisfies L/20.

rationale.a: 'a' correctly states 200 mm satisfies L/20; 'd' directly refutes the reviewer.
rationale.b: 160 mm would be too thin and non-compliant.
rationale.c: L/16 is not applicable to solid slabs; it is for ribbed beams.
rationale.correct: For a 4 m simply supported one-way solid slab, L/20 = 4000/20 = 200 mm exactly. The design is correct and meets NSCP Table 9.5.1. The reviewer's claim of non-compliance is incorrect; 200 mm IS the minimum (not 'below' it).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 6 m interior span uses a ribbed beam floor system. The structural design uses depth = 340 mm for deflection control. Is this compliant, and what is the minimum required depth per NSCP Table 9.5.1?

options.text: Non-compliant; minimum depth = 324 mm, but 340 mm is acceptable as conservative.

rationale.b: L/16 = 375 mm is for simply supported ribbed beams, not continuous.
rationale.c: Alternative ratios (L/17.6) are not permitted; use the code ratio L/21.
rationale.d: The statement is contradictory; the minimum is L/21 = 286 mm, not 324 mm.
rationale.correct: For both-ends-continuous ribbed/beam system, NSCP Table 9.5.1 specifies L/21 = 6000/21 ≈ 286 mm. The proposed 340 mm exceeds 286 mm, so it is compliant. The margin of safety is 340 – 286 = 54 mm above minimum.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A ribbed (joist) slab cantilevers 3 meters from a support. What is the minimum joist depth required per NSCP deflection control?

rationale.b: 300 mm = L/10, which is for cantilever solid slabs (not ribbed).
rationale.c: 200 mm is too thin for a 3 m cantilever.
rationale.d: 500 mm = L/6, which is thicker than required.
rationale.correct: For cantilever ribbed slabs, NSCP Table 9.5.1 specifies minimum depth = L/8. For 3 m cantilever: 3000/8 = 375 mm.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An architect proposes a simply supported one-way solid slab at 225 mm thickness for a 5 m span. Is this compliant with NSCP deflection control? If not, what is the required minimum thickness?

options.text: Compliant; 225 mm > L/20 minimum, ensuring adequate structural performance
Non-compliant; minimum thickness = 250 mm (L/20 for 5 m).
Compliant; 225 mm = L/22.2 (acceptable alternative), which meets the deflection criteria
Non-compliant; minimum thickness = 300 mm (L/16.7), necessary for heavier loads

rationale.a: 225 mm < 250 mm, so it is non-compliant.
rationale.c: Alternative ratios (L/22.2) are not permitted; code specifies the discrete value L/20.
rationale.d: L/16.7 is not a code ratio for simply supported slabs.
rationale.correct: For simply supported one-way solid slab, L/20 = 5000/20 = 250 mm. The proposed 225 mm is below this minimum and is non-compliant. The slab must be increased to 250 mm or greater to control deflection per NSCP.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A slab is one-way, solid, and one end is continuous to an adjacent span while the other end is simply supported. Which minimum thickness ratio applies per NSCP?

rationale.a: L/20 applies only when both ends are free (simply supported).
rationale.c: L/28 applies only when both ends are continuous.
rationale.d: Averaging ratios is not the code method; code specifies discrete support conditions.
rationale.correct: When one end is continuous and one end is free (simply supported), NSCP Table 9.5.1 classifies this as 'one end continuous' and requires minimum thickness = L/24 (intermediate between simply supported L/20 and both ends L/28).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.code_citation: NSCP 2015 Table 9.5.1 (One-Way Slab — One End Continuous)

questions.text: A cantilever balcony slab (one-way solid, Grade 60) extends 2.5 meters from the face of the building. What is the minimum thickness required by NSCP?

rationale.b: 200 mm = L/12.5, which is less stiff than required.
rationale.c: 150 mm = L/16.7, which is even thinner and unsafe for cantilevered elements.
rationale.d: 300 mm = L/8.3, which is thicker than required (but acceptable as conservative design).
rationale.correct: For cantilever one-way solid slabs, NSCP Table 9.5.1 specifies minimum thickness = L/10. For 2.5 m cantilever: 2500/10 = 250 mm. Cantilevers must be very stiff to limit deflection at the free end.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
